record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Is there an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical, meaning that any two computable presentations of that space are computably homeomorphic?

evidence.quote: A computable Polish space X is α-categorical if ... there is an α-computable homeomorphism ... X is (topologically) computably categorical if it is 0-categorical.
Problem 27. Is there an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A Polish space is a topological space homeomorphic to a complete separable metric space. A computable presentation of a Polish space X is a complete separable metric d on X together with a countable dense sequence (x_n)_{n in N} such that the function (i,j) |-> d(x_i, x_j) is a computable sequence of real numbers (uniformly in i,j). Two computable presentations (X, d, (x_n)) and (Y, e, (y_n)) of homeomorphic Polish spaces are said to be computably homeomorphic if there exists a homeomorphism h: X -> Y such that, viewed via the dense sequences, both h and h^{-1} are computable maps between the represented Polish spaces.

A computable Polish space X is called topologically computably categorical if any two computable presentations of X are computably homeomorphic.

Question. Does there exist an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on computable Polish spaces (Melnikov and collaborators; surveys on computable analysis and classification) characterizes computably categorical spaces in restricted classes (e.g., effectively compact spaces, Stone spaces, separable Hilbert space as a Banach space, the Urysohn space up to isometry), but the existence of an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical (categoricity up to computable homeomorphism, not just isometry) is described as a wide-open area, and no published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Computable Stone Spaces (Bazhenov, Harrison-Trainor, Melnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Computable categoricity of effectively compact Polish spaces and Polish groups up to computable homeomorphism is a wide open area.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of topological computable categoricity for Polish spaces is described as wide open.

status_evidence.title: Computable Analysis and Classification Problems
status_evidence.snippet: It would be interesting to give purely topological characterisations of categoricity in natural classes of compact Polish spaces; these problems are left open.
status_evidence.claim: Topological characterizations of computable categoricity for Polish spaces remain open.
